segments.text: A/an and the are articles. They are a type of determiner and they go before a noun.
Tenses refer to different forms of a verb or verb phrase. We use different tenses to talk or write about different times.
In a declarative clause, we expect the order to be subject – verb – object (SVO).

segments.text: Active voice is the typical word order. That is when we put the subject (the doer) first, followed by the new information (which is the focus).
The infinitive of a verb has two forms: the to-infinitive and the infinitive without to.

segments.text: Every time we use a noun we have to decide whether or not to use an article, and if we decide that an article is necessary, we then have to decide which one.

Like quantifiers, articles belong to the wider class of 'determiner', words or phrases that come at the beginning of a noun phrase and signal whether the information is new or familiar, or which tell us something about quantity.
English grammar is the set of structural rules of the English language. This includes the structure of words, phrases, clauses, sentences, and whole texts.
Linguists generally accept nine English word classes: nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, determiners, and exclamations.
For other pronouns, and all nouns, adjectives, and articles, grammatical function is indicated only by word order, by prepositions, and by the "Saxon genitive or English possessive" (-'s).
